claims.text: The FDA label reports faster release of diltiazem from extended-release capsules with alcohol in vitro, potentially increasing absorption, exposure, and dose-related adverse reactions.
claims.quote:
Alcohol: Alcohol increases the rate at which diltiazem hydrochloride extended-release capsules release diltiazem in vitro.
This effect may lead to more rapid absorption and an increase in the systemic exposure of diltiazem, and associated dose-related adverse reactions.

headline.text: The FDA label reports faster diltiazem release with alcohol in vitro and potentially increased exposure from extended-release capsules.

reported.text: The label links the faster in vitro release to potentially faster absorption, higher diltiazem exposure, and dose-related adverse reactions.

mechanism.text: Alcohol accelerates diltiazem release from the extended-release capsules in vitro.

gaps.text: The packet contains no controlled human pharmacokinetic study of alcohol with these extended-release capsules.
searched: (ethanol[tiab] OR alcohol[tiab]) AND "diltiazem"[tiab] AND (interaction OR coadministration)
